## TL;DR

Completed the requested browser QA pass for Stories, the Inbox-filtered Work queue, and Agents last-run activity at 1280px and 375px. I found no reproducible UI defect, page-level horizontal overflow, or browser console error. The only repository change is the QA record; no application code change or new regression test was warranted.

## Work and rationale

I read the task and the relevant UI workflow notes, confirmed I was in the assigned feature worktree, and used its auth-less server via `just serve-noauth 7272`. The server built the worktree's current source and started on the requested local port. I checked the named routes rather than relying on static component tests alone: `/stories`, `/work?status=inbox`, and `/agents?shotState=agents:lastRuns`.

The computer-use browser host was unavailable in this session. To continue the explicitly requested hands-on QA, I used the Playwright package already installed in this worktree and drove a headless Chromium page against the same local server. I checked page errors and console messages, measured the rendered document width at both target viewport widths, and captured temporary screenshots for inspection. I did not claim results from a real-device browser.

At 1280px, all three routes rendered without document-width overflow. At 375px, Stories remained within the viewport and the story panel opened as an overlay. The Inbox quick filter accepted a P2 selection and the visible task count updated. Opening an Inbox task displayed the phone task-detail layout with queue return and close controls, status selection, move action, and the task's human/input notices. On the Agents page, the `agents:lastRuns` fixture populated recent-run statuses; opening a failed status displayed the failure reason and task-log link within the viewport. No browser console errors or uncaught page errors were observed in these passes.

Stories' completed-story filter also responded after the asynchronously loaded story list had rendered. The populated repository did not provide an empty Stories state during the browser pass. Existing `stories-view.test.ts` tests cover the disabled state and a registered story with no tasks, so I recorded that limit rather than representing it as a live empty-state observation.

The only horizontal scrolling observed at 375px was inside the Work queue's quick-filter strip. That strip contains priority and area/story controls and is deliberately implemented as an internal scroll region; the document itself stayed at 375px. The failed-run details on Agents fit within the viewport. These observations did not point to a specific reproducible defect, so adding a source change or a test would have introduced speculative behavior rather than fixing a demonstrated problem.

## Approaches tried

I started with the repository's `repoos outline` summaries to identify the Stories, Work, and Agents implementations and existing Stories tests without reading large files wholesale. I launched the auth-less server from the assigned worktree, then visited the three routes at desktop width and at 375px. The agent activity route used the existing `agents:lastRuns` preview fixture to make success, failure, and previous-setup states observable without modifying repository data.

I opened a story panel and a task detail drawer at phone width, expanded a failed agent-run status, selected P2 in the Inbox quick filters, and toggled Hide Completed Stories. I also inspected screenshots of the mobile list and drawer states. The first list count probe ran before Stories data finished loading, so I reran the filter interaction after the list had rendered; the filter then visibly changed the story card count. This was a timing adjustment in the QA probe, not a product bug.

## Challenges and blockers

The CUA browser host returned an unavailable error, so its browser UI could not be used. The installed Playwright runtime was available and allowed the requested route, viewport, interaction, screenshot, and console checks to proceed locally. This fallback is noted in the QA record. The server's repository data contained populated stories, which limited live validation of an actually empty Stories route; I recorded that limitation and relied on the existing view tests for the disabled and zero-task cases.

No other blocker prevented the pass. The server stayed worktree-local, and I did not alter `repoos.toml`, task metadata, or repository data.

## Key learnings

The current phone layouts remain within the viewport for the sampled stories, inbox, and agent activity content. The Work quick-filter strip is intentionally horizontally scrollable and should be evaluated as an inner control rail rather than page overflow. The Agents fixture is useful for exercising last-run error details without requiring a real agent run. The current repository data is suitable for populated Stories and Inbox paths, while empty Stories states are better verified through the existing component tests unless a dedicated browser fixture is added in a future task.

The QA notes are in `docs/qa/2026-11-stories-inbox.md`. RepoOS can bind this report draft to the checked tree when it finalizes the handoff.
